title: Time Tested Tradition
notes: This chunk is dense, assertive, and on-voice: the map/terrain frame, the chained NT charges against Pharisaic tradition, and the eclipse-anchored AD 32 claim land with force and without hedging. Main defects are house-style sentence openers (multiple author-prose lines begin with But/And/That), residual presenter imperatives built on “weigh,” one clear comma splice, and a slightly broken “puts a Monday crucifixion” construction. TimeTested.Bible also appears in body prose, which house style reserves for front/back matter or footnotes; one residual “And when…” opener remains after the fixes below.

proposals.old: But if we can definitively identify the years, the months, and the days of the week on which certain events occurred, then we can see what calendar — if any — matches the historical testimony.
proposals.new: If we can definitively identify the years, the months, and the days of the week on which certain events occurred, then we can see what calendar — if any — matches the historical testimony.
proposals.summary: Remove prohibited sentence-initial But in author prose.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author-prose sentences that open with And/But/That. Dropping the conjunction keeps the claim intact and assertive.

proposals.old: On the known dates, none of the known weekly sabbaths align with Saturday; the year of the cross puts a *Monday* crucifixion — an impossibility for rising on the third day after three days and three nights.
proposals.new: On the known dates, none of the known weekly sabbaths align with Saturday; the year of the cross puts the crucifixion on a *Monday* — an impossibility for rising on the third day after three days and three nights.
proposals.summary: Repair awkward “puts a Monday crucifixion” phrasing.
proposals.rationale: The original is compressed past natural English and briefly obscures the claim. The rewrite states the same fact in ordinary word order without adding doctrine.

proposals.old: Before weighing the evidence, weigh the witnesses, for Scripture itself commands it.
proposals.new: The witnesses must be weighed before the evidence, for Scripture itself commands it.
proposals.rationale: House style bans presenter staging such as “Weigh the.” The replacement keeps the same legal-testimony force in third-person assertion.

proposals.old: And if Scripture declares a sect to be children of the father of lies, how can its testimony be received?
proposals.new: If Scripture declares a sect to be children of the father of lies, how can its testimony be received?
proposals.rationale: Author prose may not open with And. The rhetorical question stands without the conjunction.

proposals.old: When that testimony is put on the stand, weigh what it actually brings.
proposals.new: When that testimony is put on the stand, what it actually brings must be weighed.
proposals.rationale: The imperative addresses the reader as a stage direction. Passive assertion preserves the courtroom image and the demand to test the witnesses.

proposals.old: the writings of the losing side are not archived by the winners, they are neglected and destroyed.
proposals.new: the writings of the losing side are not archived by the winners; they are neglected and destroyed.
proposals.rationale: Two independent clauses were joined by a comma. A semicolon is the minimal correct join and keeps the cadence.

proposals.old: That same argument from silence once dismissed the house of David as legend — until the Tel Dan stone surfaced in 1993 with __“House of David”__ cut into it; and Pontius Pilate — until his stone came out of the ground at Caesarea in 1961.
proposals.new: The same argument from silence once dismissed the house of David as legend — until the Tel Dan stone surfaced in 1993 with __“House of David”__ cut into it; and Pontius Pilate — until his stone came out of the ground at Caesarea in 1961.
proposals.rationale: House style bars author-prose openings with That. “The same” keeps the anaphora and the archaeological punch.

proposals.old: And God did not appoint the map — He appointed the terrain: __“let them be for sym:sym-sign[signs], and for seasons”__ — for _moedim_, the appointed times — __“and for days, and years”__ (Genesis 1:14), spoken of the lights in the firmament, which have kept perfect time through every century in which the maps were redrawn.
proposals.new: God did not appoint the map — He appointed the terrain: __“let them be for sym:sym-sign[signs], and for seasons”__ — for _moedim_, the appointed times — __“and for days, and years”__ (Genesis 1:14), spoken of the lights in the firmament, which have kept perfect time through every century in which the maps were redrawn.
proposals.summary: Remove prohibited sentence-initial And before the Genesis claim.
proposals.rationale: Opening with And violates house style. The map/terrain contrast and the Genesis 1:14 citation remain unchanged and stronger without the conjunction.
